title: Trivial geometric stabilizers of a Deligne--Mumford stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$, in the groupoid and stack conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Assume that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, and every $x\in\mathcal X(\Omega)$, the automorphism group of $x$ is trivial. Then $\mathcal X$ is naturally equivalent to the discrete groupoid of points of an algebraic space $E$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. In particular every object of $\mathcal X(T)$ has only the identity automorphism for every $S$-scheme $T$, including nonreduced $T$.

source.place: Tag 04SZ, proposition-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms; DM geometric-stabilizer corollary using the unramified diagonal (stacks-morphisms.tex, definition of DM) and Tag 05W1, spaces-morphisms.tex lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism. The identity section of the unramified inertia is an open immersion, surjective when geometric stabilizers are trivial.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$, an object $x\in\mathcal X(T)$, and an automorphism $\alpha:x\xrightarrow{\sim}x$. Apply [lem-sfb-dm-isom-space-unramified] to $(x,x)$. Thus $A=\operatorname{Isom}_T(x,x)$ is an algebraic space, unramified over $T$, whose $T'$-points are the automorphisms of $x_{T'}$. The identity and $\alpha$ define two sections $e,a:T\to A$.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), (3) implies (1), and Tag 06MB (lemma-properties-covering-imply-diagonal); Isom base-change description in algebraic.tex Tag 045G.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal] to $A\to T$ and to the morphism $(a,e):T\to A\times_T A$. Its pullback of the diagonal is an open subscheme $j:W\hookrightarrow T$. For every $u:T'\to T$, the defining fibre-product condition says that $u$ factors through $W$ exactly when $\alpha|_{T'}=\operatorname{id}_{x_{T'}}$. This is equality as arrows, with their full scheme structures retained.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1), pulled back by the ordered pair of sections.

proof.text: For any point $t\in T$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ exists by the residue-field description in [def-weil-geometric-point]. The hypothesis applied to the pullback of $x$ along $\bar t$ gives $\alpha|_{\bar t}=\operatorname{id}$. Hence $\bar t$ factors through $W$, so $t\in|W|$. Thus $|W|=|T|$. By the definition of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], $W$ has the restricted structure sheaf on this same open set and $j$ is an isomorphism. The equality defining $W$ now yields $\alpha=\operatorname{id}_x$. Since $T,x,\alpha$ were arbitrary, all fibre automorphism groups are trivial, including when $T$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), open-equalizer argument applied to the geometric stabilizer hypothesis; the conclusion uses only the definition of an open subscheme, not a reducedness assumption.

proof.text: Define $F(T)$ to be the set of isomorphism classes of $\mathcal X(T)$, with restrictions induced by pullback. For any two arrows $f,g:x\to y$ in a fibre groupoid, $g^{-1}f$ is an automorphism of $x$, so the preceding step gives $f=g$. In the stack convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], matching isomorphism classes on an etale cover therefore have unique isomorphisms on overlaps; the two composites on each triple overlap agree because there is at most one arrow. Effective descent gives an object on $T$. Any two such objects are uniquely isomorphic: the local isomorphisms agree on overlaps by uniqueness and glue by the sheaf property for isomorphisms. This proves the etale sheaf axiom for $F$. The canonical functor $\mathcal X(T)\to F(T)$, with $F(T)$ a discrete groupoid, is fully faithful (each Hom is empty or a singleton) and essentially surjective (every class has a representative). These functors commute with pullback, giving an equivalence over $\mathit{Sch}/S$.

source.place: Tag 045H (lemma-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms), proof of (1) implies (3): passage to the sheaf of isomorphism classes; the descent and equivalence arguments are written out here for the given etale-stack convention.

proof.text: Choose the surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$ furnished by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and compose it with the preceding equivalence to obtain $q:h_U\to F$. Given $a\in F(T)$, choose a representative $x\in\mathcal X(T)$. On a $T$-scheme $T'$, a point of $h_T\times_F h_U$ is a map $v:T'\to U$ for which $p(v)$ and $x|_{T'}$ have the same isomorphism class. There is then exactly one isomorphism $p(v)\xrightarrow{\sim}x|_{T'}$. Thus adding this isomorphism, or forgetting it, are inverse identifications with the points of $T\times_{\mathcal X}U$. They respect restriction since the isomorphism is unique. By the atlas hypothesis this fibre product is an algebraic space and its map to $T$ is surjective etale. This verifies the atlas condition for $F$ on every test scheme; a change of representative $x$ gives the same identification through its unique isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 045H (lemma-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms), proof of (1) implies (3): transferring the atlas to the sheaf. The identification of the ordinary fibre product and the 2-fibre product is written explicitly using unique isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-etale-sheaf-space-atlas-bootstrap] to the etale sheaf $F$ and the atlas $q:h_U\to F$ just checked. It gives an algebraic space $E$ over $S$ whose functor of points is $F$, in particular an fppf sheaf. Compose this identification with the canonical equivalence in step 4. This is the required natural equivalence of $\mathcal X$ with the discrete groupoid of points of $E$. The assertion about automorphisms on every $T$, including nonreduced $T$, was already proved in step 3.

source.place: Tag 0BH4 (lemma-spaces-etale-locally-representable), with the atlas a scheme. This explicitly bridges etale sheaves to the fppf algebraic-space convention.

proof_origin.place: Tag 045H (lemma-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms), proof of (1) implies (3), and Tag 04SZ (proposition-algebraic-stack-no-automorphisms); preceded by the open-equalizer argument from spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W1, using stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06N3. The etale/fppf convention is bridged by bootstrap.tex Tag 0BH4.
